2	
3	This task is based on the real `deepmodeling/dpti` workflow for atomic-liquid
4	Hamiltonian thermodynamic integration. The software constructs simulation
5	inputs for a path between a reference interaction and a target atomistic model.
6	The benchmark does not require running a molecular-dynamics simulation; the
7	scientific question is whether the generated input preserves the meaning of the
8	intended path.
9	
10	## Scientific context
11	
12	Hamiltonian thermodynamic integration describes a family of systems through a
13	coupling parameter. Quantities reported along that path must remain physically
14	interpretable when the parameter approaches the boundary of its allowed range.
15	An expression that only appears reasonable away from the boundary is not a
16	valid definition of the observable for the whole path.
17	
18	The observable used by a free-energy workflow must represent the energy change
19	associated with the interaction being changed. It must not silently switch to a
20	different normalization or sign convention when the direction of the path is
21	reversed.
22	
23	For a mixture, an interaction is defined for each chemically distinct pair of
24	element types. A compact shared-parameter representation and a representation
25	with a separate value for each pair are both legitimate, but they describe
26	different data models. The generated workflow must preserve the chosen model:
27	it must neither merge distinct pair values nor refer to a value that was not
28	defined.
29	
30	Soft reference interactions are commonly used to make difficult free-energy
31	paths numerically tractable. The boundary of the soft-reference path is still a
32	scientific state in the workflow, not an invalid special case that may be
33	silently omitted.

Done. The missing capability was the `protect_eps` endpoint protection of the coupling path in the atomic-liquid HTI workflow.

## Diagnosis

The liquid integrator defines the sampled observable as `e_diff = c_lj_pe/v_LAMBDA` in the `soft_on` stage and `e_diff = -c_lj_pe/v_INV_LAMBDA` in the `soft_off` stage (`source/dpti/hti_liq.py:102,152`). Because the soft reference interaction is itself switched off exactly at the path endpoint, these expressions become 0/0 there — visible in the generated `outputs/boundary_case_a.lammps` (λ=0) and `boundary_case_b.lammps` (λ=1) artifacts. No raw estimator can fix this at the endpoint; the workflow's own documented mechanism is to protect the integration grid instead, keeping the same normalization and sign convention in both path directions:

- The bundled README documents `protect_eps` ("the minimum lambda number used in numerical integration") as a field of `hti.liquid.json` (`source/README.md:555`).
- Sibling modules apply it: `hti.py:649,675-678` (uniform protection of every stage's grid) and `hti_water.py:205-217`.
- `dpti/lib/utils.py:159-181` `parse_seq` carries a `protect_eps` keyword implementing exactly that protection — but had no caller left in the snapshot.

Only `hti_liq.py::_make_tasks` had lost the handling.

## Fix

`source/dpti/hti_liq.py::_make_tasks` now reads `protect_eps = jdata["protect_eps"]` and passes it to `parse_seq(..., protect_eps=protect_eps)` for all three stages (`soft_on`, `deep_on`, `soft_off`), mirroring `hti.py`'s uniform treatment. Five lines, no API or signature changes, no hard-coded values — the grid shift is value- and element-count-agnostic, so mixtures with pair-specific `sigma_i_j`/`epsilon_i_j`/`activation_i_j` keep every distinct pair value and never reference undefined keys.

## Verification

- Public reproduction: all five artifacts under `outputs/` are byte-identical to before (`reproduce.py` calls the raw single-input generator directly, intentionally bypassing task-grid construction; public APIs and interior behavior preserved).
- End-to-end `make_tasks` with boundary-inclusive grids on a binary mixture: `soft_on` first task λ=1e-06 (was 0), `soft_off` last task λ=0.999999 (was 1), interior points unshifted, `lambda.out` consistent for the post-integration, and all distinct pair coefficients preserved verbatim.
- Regression sweep: 36 generator variants (3 stages × 1–3 elements × shared/per-pair parameterizations × deepmd/meam backends) unchanged; invalid mixed parameter models and unknown stages still rejected loudly; `parse_seq` protection verified across all supported input forms (arange strings, float lists, single strings).
